reference.time: ET/TDB seconds internally; UTC converted using packaged SPICE mapping
reference.dynamics: GL1800F degree 30 DE440 PA full lunar gravity + differential Earth/Sun point masses from DE440 for ALL phases; finite constant thrust for departure/insertion/DOI, piecewise acceleration for descent, and integrated mass flow

reference_seed.label: NASA/JSC 2018 reference NRHO state; browser repropagation in simplified DE440 Earth-Moon-Sun model
reference_seed.provenance: Geometric spkezr(-60000, epoch, J2000, NONE, MOON). SPK original origin is Earth, transformed using DE440s. Not a flown/operational ephemeris.
reference_seed.source_force_model: Published reference uses DE430, DE431 GMs, Earth/Moon/Sun/Jupiter and lunar 8x8 gravity plus small stationkeeping impulses.
reference_seed.runtime_force_model: The browser starts only from this state and propagates lunar monopole plus differential Earth/Sun attraction. No source stationkeeping impulses are imported; no exact periodicity is assumed.

warnings: Terminal envelope demo-terminal-v1 uses assumed limits and a 2 m radial contact proxy. It does not validate attitude dynamics, landing legs, slopes or unresolved obstacles.
MODE B — NASA dated reference initial condition propagated in the selected Earth/Moon/Sun model; not an operational Gateway ephemeris.
The source reference trajectory includes other forces and maintenance maneuvers; only its documented initial state is reused. No later source samples replace the integrated trajectory.

Departure, insertion and DOI integrate finite maximum-thrust burns with fixed inertial direction and variable mass. Attitude, slew, ignition transients, navigation uncertainty and operational certification remain outside this model.
GL1800F is a truncated static measured gravity model. Degree 2/3 permanent tides are excluded in the source; small numerical residuals do not establish actual landing accuracy.
Reference preview extrema are extrema of the computed time window, not a proof of periodicity.
LOLA terrain validation is limited to the supplied 240 m south-polar DEM.
